parts.text: Which claim correctly explains how these human actions create major threats to life on Earth?

options.text: They disturb living and non-living systems: greenhouse gases trap more heat, and habitat loss and pollution harm ecosystems and people.
Burning fossil fuels cools Earth, so it cannot threaten life.
Habitat destruction affects only rocks, never plants or animals.
Pollution is only a brief smell and cannot harm crops, water, or soil.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Neil lists burning fossil fuels, clearing natural habitats, and releasing pollutants into air, water, and soil.

part_answers.answer: Human actions release greenhouse gases, destroy habitats, and pollute, disturbing Earth-system balance and threatening life.

teacher.key_rationale: Human actions threaten life by disturbing connected systems through greenhouse gases, habitat loss, and pollution. Claiming fossil fuels cool Earth, habitats affect only rocks, or pollution cannot harm crops and water all miss that hinge.
